newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico reiterates to privatize petrochemicals.
newsitem.headline: Mexico reiterates to privatize petrochemicals.

text.p: The Mexican government reiterated on Friday that it intends to move ahead with its long-delayed plans to privatize the petrochemical industry, despite recent opposition expressed within the ranks of the ruling party.
"The government has not suspended the process of privatizing the secobdary petrochemical industry," Energy Minister Jesus Reyes Heroles told journalists.

Reyes nonetheless said the government was holding talks with members of the Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI), some of whose rank-and-file members expressed vocal opposition to privatization plans at a party conference last weekend.
The government will review the party's objections "to a full and fair extent," he said.
Adrian Lajous, CEO of Mexico's state-owned oil corporation Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) said on Wednesday the government had yet to issue guidelines for the privatization process.

"Pemex awaits specific indications from the authorities on this issue," Lajous said, following a meeting with legislators. Reyes agreed with remarks by Lajous that delays in privatization had held up public and private investments in the petrochemical industry.
"A series of domestic and foreign investment projects have unfortunately been halted as secondary petrochemical plant sales have not been finalized," he said.
The PRI, in power since 1929, held a conference last Sunday that approved a motion defending Mexican crude oil and all solid, liquid and gas hydrocarbons as "property of the nation."
But delegates said that a motion expressly forbidding the sale of petrochemical plants was left out of the final draft of the conference's resolutions.
Reyes said on Friday that reporting of the conference had led to "enormous confusion."
"In every government in the world there are differences with the parties that bring them to power," he added.
